name: listing-icon-after-semicolon
story: In semicolon-separated info listings (hours, phone, transit), the model predicts the next single-letter field-marker token such as ' t', ' h', or ' %'.

name: post-comma-continuation
story: Immediately after a comma the model predicts the lowercase word that opens the next list item or clause.

name: preposition-after-noun-phrase
story: After completing a noun phrase the model predicts a common preposition (at, in, of, with) that attaches a location, time, or complement.

name: indefinite-article
story: After a verb, comma, or quantifier the model opens a new noun phrase by predicting the indefinite article 'a' or 'an'.

name: the-before-adjective
story: Right after the definite article 'the' the model predicts a lowercase modifier or noun beginning the noun phrase.

name: verb-after-to-or-modal
story: After an infinitive marker, modal, relative pronoun, or coordinator the model predicts the following base verb.

name: paren-close-plus-punct
story: The model closes a parenthetical with a bracket token that is fused with trailing punctuation or preceded by a space, which the plain bracket-close rule misses.

name: preposition-attachment
story: The model predicts a common preposition attaching to the noun phrase or verb just completed (e.g. 'example of', 'miles for', 'eatery on').

name: prep-object-start
story: Immediately after a preposition, the model launches the object noun phrase (e.g. 'state of flux', 'headland in snow', 'owned by an').

name: after-semicolon-field
story: In semicolon-delimited listing lines (addresses, hours, prices common in web directories), the model predicts the next field's opening token right after the semicolon.

name: determiner-launch
story: After a verb or preposition the model opens a fresh noun phrase with a determiner or possessive (e.g. 'open during the', 'guard your', 'tick all').

name: word-after-determiner
story: Directly after an article or demonstrative, the model predicts the first content word of the noun phrase (e.g. 'along the white', 'A taxi', 'at this venue').

name: numeral-onset
story: The model starts a new number after a non-numeric token, as in prices, addresses, years, and phone numbers ('slated for a 2016', 'call 08', 'is 13 miles').

name: copula-predicate-start
story: Right after a form of 'to be', the model begins the predicate or complement (e.g. 'It was later', 'Daunt is one', 'guides are also').

name: finite-verb-launch
story: After a subject pronoun, relative pronoun, quantifier, or pre-verbal adverb/negation, the model predicts the clause's main verb (e.g. 'which has', 'also find', 'not suit', 'some accept').

name: preposition-linker
story: A common function preposition attaches a complement or modifier to the preceding noun or verb phrase (e.g. 'fares in', 'known as', 'ambling through', 'prices for').

name: of-genitive-object
story: The word right after 'of' completes a genitive or fixed phrase ('Houses of Parliament', 'coach of 17..', 'of course', 'exception of London').

name: proper-noun-after-comma
story: In addresses and lists, a comma is followed by a new capitalized proper-noun component such as a street, district, or postcode ('Green Street, Upton', 'Belvedere Rd, SE1').

name: number-start-after-preposition
story: A fresh number (a year, hour, or count) begins immediately after a preposition or determiner ('in the 19th century', 'coach of 17..', 'to 6pm', 'to 9pm').

name: opening-hours-token
story: Business-listing opening-hours strings continue with a highly predictable schedule token: a weekday abbreviation after a time or ampersand, 'noon', or the hours-marker 'h' ('10am-5pm Tue', 'Sat & Sun', 'hgrill noon').

name: selected-preposition
story: A verb, noun, or adjective that lexically selects a particular preposition makes the model predict it, e.g. 'head[-> to]', 'popular[-> with]', 'heart[-> of]', 'dating[-> from]'.

name: listing-delimiter
story: Inside compact non-prose material such as phone numbers, URLs, prices, and abbreviations, the model predicts the next delimiter character, e.g. '%020[->-]', 'adult[->/]', 'http[->://]', 'B[->&]B'.

name: cap-after-clause-punct
story: Immediately after a period or comma the model predicts a capitalized word that opens the next sentence or the next item in a list, e.g. 'bathrooms.[-> Wonderful]', 'Liverpool,[-> Carl]isle', 'festivals,[-> Field]'.

name: noun-after-hyphenated-modifier
story: After a hyphenated compound modifier such as 'tablet-controlled', 'tucked-away', '12th-century', or 'line-caught', the model predicts the head noun the compound modifies.
